t: Viatina-19 FIV Mara Imóveis, a Nelore Cow
d: A snow-white Nelore cow weighing about 1,100 kg, roughly twice the size of an average adult of her breed. She is prized for fast muscle growth and fertility. A one-third share sold at auction, valuing the whole cow at this price.
f: Guinness World Records lists her as the most expensive cow ever sold at auction, at more than three times the previous record. Her owners put up highway billboards advertising her.

t: An Old Master Painting of Christ as Salvator Mundi
d: A walnut panel of Christ holding a crystal orb, attributed to Leonardo da Vinci. It was once sold as a copy for about £45.
f: It's the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction, and it hasn't been seen in public since.

d: One of the best-preserved Stradivari violins, named after Lord Byron's granddaughter, who owned it.
f: The proceeds went to relief after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan.

d: Six pairs of game-worn sneakers, one from each of Jordan's six championship-clinching Finals games.
The only known white-gold example of this vintage Daytona reference, from the collection of a famous Rolex scholar.
f: Collectors call it the Unicorn because it is one of a kind.

d: One of two known $20 gold coins with an experimental tall-lettered reverse design.
A custom guitar built by luthier Doug Irwin with a tiger inlay. It was the Grateful Dead guitarist's main instrument for years.
f: The estimate was $1–2 million.

d: The largest Triceratops ever found, about 26 feet long, discovered in South Dakota.
f: It's the most expensive dinosaur ever sold in Europe.

t: First Printing of the United States Constitution
d: One of only two privately owned copies of the first official printing, made for the convention delegates.
f: A crypto collective, ConstitutionDAO, raised over $40 million online to buy it, and lost to a hedge-fund chief.

t: F.P. Journe 'FFC Blue', Made for Francis Ford Coppola
d: A unique prototype in which a small articulated hand shows the hours. It was conceived with the film director.
A gold pocket watch commissioned by a New York banker in a rivalry to own the world's most complicated watch.
f: It's the most expensive pocket watch ever sold at auction.

t: A 1962 Ferrari 250 GTO, Sold at Mecum
d: A 250 GTO offered at a large public car auction in Florida, not at a boutique sale.
A gold coin struck by New York goldsmith Ephraim Brasher, stamped with his 'EB' hallmark on the eagle's wing.
A two-year-old hen from a famous Antwerp loft, named the best young bird in Belgium in 2018. Bidding opened at €200.
f: Two Chinese bidders using the handles 'Super Duper' and 'Hitman' fought over her in the final half hour.

d: One of 48 commemorative copies signed by Abraham Lincoln, later owned by Robert F. Kennedy.
A bottle from the same legendary 1926 cask, with the distillery's own label.
A nine-year-old, roughly one-metre female koi with the classic red-and-white Kōhaku pattern.
f: A collector from Taiwan won the bidding.

d: A 1953 letter to his twelve-year-old son explaining the newly discovered structure of DNA.

t: Andy Warhol, Shot Sage Blue Marilyn
d: A 1964 silkscreen of Marilyn Monroe from a series of portraits made two years after her death.
f: It held the auction record for any 20th-century artwork until the Klimt in this catalogue broke it.

t: A 1961 Ferrari 250 GT SWB California Spyder 'Barn Find'
d: Found in a French barn under stacks of old magazines, part of a forgotten collection of about sixty cars.
f: It once belonged to the French actor Alain Delon.

t: Steve McQueen's 'Le Mans' Camera Car, a 1968 Ford GT40
d: A GT40 used as a camera car to film racing scenes for Steve McQueen's 1971 film 'Le Mans'.
The largest internally flawless vivid pink diamond ever graded, the size of a plum.
f: It's the most expensive gemstone ever sold at auction, at about $1.2 million per carat.

d: Sixty years in sherry cask, one of twelve bottles with a label painted by Valerio Adami.
f: It's the most expensive bottle of wine or spirits ever sold at auction.

t: Louis Vuitton × Yayoi Kusama Pumpkin Minaudière
d: A polka-dotted, pumpkin-shaped evening bag made for the brand's collaboration with the Japanese artist.
f: The estimate was $10,000–15,000.

d: The 1938 debut of Superman, which sold for ten cents on the newsstand. This is the 'Kansas City' pedigree copy.
f: Only about a hundred copies are thought to survive, out of 200,000 printed.

d: A $20 gold coin from a mintage that was almost entirely melted down. It is the only one that can legally be privately owned.
f: It was once owned by King Farouk of Egypt.

d: A single bottle from the last vintage before the domaine's old vines were replanted. Only about six hundred bottles were made.
f: It's the most expensive bottle of wine ever sold at auction.

d: A street lit by a single lamp at night, under a bright daytime sky. Magritte returned to this theme throughout his career.
f: It set new auction records for Magritte and for any Surrealist work.

d: A V12 sports racer raced in the Mille Miglia, later owned by a French collector for decades.
A small Birkin in lizard skin dyed to fade from light to dark.
A unique silver pattern coin from Manchuria, known as the 'King of Chinese Coins'.
f: It's the most expensive non-American coin ever sold at auction.

t: James Naismith's Original Rules of Basketball
d: Two typed pages from 1891 setting out the thirteen original rules of the game, which Naismith invented.
The red Chicago jersey from Game One of the 1998 Finals, his 'Last Dance' season.
A 33-carat Asscher-cut diamond ring that Richard Burton gave Taylor, who wore it almost every day.
A road car with three seats in a row and the driver in the middle, bought new by its owner and barely driven.
Called the 'King of American Coins', this dollar was actually struck in the 1830s for diplomatic gift sets.

house: Toyosu Market New Year auction, Tokyo
d: A 278 kg Pacific bluefin from Ōma, sold at the first auction ever held at Toyosu after the old Tsukiji market moved.
f: The buyer, a sushi chain, still served it at regular menu prices. It went for ¥333.6 million.

d: One of ten convertibles built for Ferrari's North American dealer, owned by the same family since 1968.
f: The proceeds went to charity.

d: A 14.62-carat vivid blue diamond, named for a member of the De Beers mining family.

t: Patek Philippe Ref. 1518 in Pink Gold
d: A pink-gold perpetual-calendar chronograph originally made for an Egyptian prince.

t: A Pair of Ruby Slippers from 'The Wizard of Oz'
d: Sequined pumps worn by Judy Garland. This pair was stolen from a museum in 2005 and recovered by the FBI in 2018.
f: The estimate was $3 million. Phone bidders battled for about fifteen minutes.

d: A unique stainless-steel example of Patek's most complicated wristwatch, with twenty complications and a reversible case, made for a charity sale.
f: It's the most expensive wristwatch ever sold at auction.

d: One of thirty-six 250 GTOs built. Collectors widely consider it the ultimate collector's car.
A 12.03-carat vivid blue cushion-cut diamond, found in South Africa in 2014.
f: The buyer, a Hong Kong billionaire, renamed it after his daughter.

t: Pablo Picasso, Femme à la montre
d: A 1932 portrait of Picasso's lover and muse Marie-Thérèse Walter, seated and wearing a wristwatch.
f: It came from the collection of philanthropist Emily Fisher Landau.

d: The largest and most complete T. rex known at the time. It was the first dinosaur ever sold at auction.
f: Chicago's Field Museum bought it with corporate sponsors, and it still stands there today.

d: Ferrari's own factory team car, raced at Le Mans and in period endurance races.
f: It's the most expensive Ferrari ever sold at auction.

d: The only known example of this ten-cent piece struck at the Carson City mint.

t: A 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle Card, SGC 9.5
d: The most iconic post-war baseball card, in near-mint condition.
f: Topps once dumped unsold 1952 cards in the ocean to clear warehouse space.

t: The Wicked Witch of the West's Hat
d: Margaret Hamilton's black pointed hat from 'The Wizard of Oz', matched to her first scene in the film.
f: It sold in the same sale as the ruby slippers.

t: A Himalaya Niloticus Crocodile Birkin 30 with Diamonds
d: Matte white crocodile shading into smoky grey, with 18-karat white gold and diamond hardware.
f: Collectors call the Himalaya the most coveted bag Hermès makes.

d: One of three known 1822 $5 gold coins. The other two are in the Smithsonian.
A lavishly illuminated Flemish book of hours from around 1505.
The car Hamilton drove to his first win for Mercedes, at the 2013 Hungarian Grand Prix.
A bass-drum head bearing the Beatles' famous logo.
A reclining nude from the artist's celebrated 1917–18 series, which scandalised Paris when first shown.
f: Police closed Modigliani's only solo show, which included nudes from this series, on the opening day.

d: Jane Birkin's own black leather Birkin 40, well worn on her travels.
f: It's the second most expensive Birkin ever sold.

t: Kurt Cobain's 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' Fender Mustang
d: The left-handed 1969 Mustang seen in the music video for Nirvana's breakthrough single.
f: Cobain liked Mustangs partly because few quality guitars were made for left-handed players.

t: Bob Dylan's 'Like a Rolling Stone' Lyrics
d: Four pages of hotel stationery with Dylan's pencilled draft of his 1965 hit.
A pear-shaped natural pearl found in the 16th century, once owned by Spanish and English queens. Richard Burton gave it to Taylor.
f: Taylor once lost it in a hotel suite and found her puppy chewing on it.

d: An acoustic played on 'Help!'-era recordings that was lost for over fifty years.
f: It turned up in an attic in the English countryside.

d: A pedigree Texel lamb sold for breeding at the Scottish national sale, beating the previous sheep record by more than £130,000.
f: It sold for 350,000 guineas, the traditional currency of British livestock auctions.

d: The Argentina shirt from the 1986 World Cup quarter-final against England, when he scored with his hand and then a famous solo goal.
f: England's Steve Hodge kept it after swapping shirts at the end of the match.

t: The Original Birkin Bag, from Jane Birkin
d: The prototype Hermès made for the actress after she complained about her bag to the company's chief executive on a flight.
f: It's the most expensive handbag ever sold at auction.

d: A handwritten Prelude, Fugue and Allegro for lute or harpsichord, one of very few Bach manuscripts in private hands.

t: John Lennon's Psychedelic 1965 Rolls-Royce Phantom V
d: A black limousine Lennon had repainted in swirling Romany-caravan colours in 1967.
f: It was bought by Canadian businessman Jim Pattison, who later donated it to a museum in British Columbia.

d: The 1623 collection that preserved eighteen of Shakespeare's plays that would otherwise have been lost.
f: It's the most expensive work of literature ever sold at auction.

t: Georges Seurat, Les Poseuses, Ensemble (Petite version)
d: A pointillist painting of three models in the artist's studio, painted in tiny dots of pure colour.
f: It was offered from the collection of Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen, whose collection sale raised over $1.5 billion.

d: Signed, game-worn sneakers from Game Two of the 1998 Finals.
f: It's the most expensive pair of game-worn sneakers ever sold at auction.

d: The left-handed 1959 acoustic-electric he played at the 1993 Unplugged taping.
f: The buyer, a microphone-company founder, later lent it to the Royal College of Music.

d: A streamlined Formula One car with fully enclosed bodywork, raced in the 1950s Mercedes Silver Arrows era.
f: It's the most expensive Formula One car ever sold at auction.

d: André Breton's handwritten 1924 manuscript that launched the Surrealist movement.
An acoustic-electric Lennon used for early Beatles songs. It went missing in 1963.
The final canvas in a fifteen-part series painted in homage to Delacroix, filled with fractured, colourful figures.
f: At the time, it set the auction record for any artwork.

d: A two-crown world-time wristwatch double-signed by the Milan retailer Gobbi, with an enamel map dial.
A red, white and black striped guitar Van Halen built from parts, descended from his famous 'Frankenstein'.

t: Francis Bacon, Three Studies of Lucian Freud
d: A 1969 triptych of the painter's friend and rival, seated on a chair inside a cage-like frame.
f: At the time, it was the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction.

d: The ball from McGwire's record-setting 70th home run of the 1998 season.
f: The buyer was comic-book creator Todd McFarlane.

t: Paul Newman's Own Rolex Daytona, Ref. 6239
d: A steel chronograph engraved on the caseback by Joanne Woodward for her husband, the actor and racing driver.
f: It's the most expensive watch ever sold at auction in North America.

t: Caxton's First Edition of The Canterbury Tales
d: Chaucer's tales as printed by William Caxton in 1477, one of the first books printed in England.

t: A Gold Dinar of Caliph Yazid II, AD 723
d: An early Islamic gold coin said to be struck from gold from the caliph's own mine near Mecca.

t: 'Love is in the Bin', a Shredded Canvas
d: A painting of a girl with a heart-shaped balloon that shredded itself in its frame moments after the hammer fell in 2018.
f: In 2018 the buyer paid about £1 million. Three years later the half-shredded work sold for roughly eighteen times that.

t: Babe Ruth's 1932 'Called Shot' World Series Jersey
d: The road jersey from the game in which Ruth is said to have pointed to centre field and then homered there.
f: It's the most expensive piece of sports memorabilia ever sold at auction.

d: The handwritten 14-page speech from 1892 in which the founder of the modern Olympics proposed reviving the Games.
The acoustic Clapton played on his 1992 'Unplugged' album.
f: It's the most ever paid for a Martin acoustic. In 2004 it sold for $791,500.

d: Twenty-seven graduated emerald-green jadeite beads, a wedding gift to the heiress Barbara Hutton.
f: It's the most expensive jadeite jewel ever sold.

d: One of only four known 1940s perpetual-calendar chronographs in steel. The model usually came in gold.
The ivory halter dress that billows up over a subway grate in 'The Seven Year Itch'.
A JPEG collage of every image the artist posted online each day for more than thirteen years, sold as an NFT.
f: Bidding opened at $100. It was Christie's first purely digital artwork.

d: One of the few surviving pitch books for a legendary unmade 1970s film adaptation of 'Dune'.
f: The buyers thought it gave them film rights. It didn't.

t: Gustav Klimt, Dame mit Fächer (Lady with a Fan)
d: Klimt's last portrait: a woman against a gold-and-turquoise background of birds and flowers, still on his easel when he died in 1918.
A red knitted sweater with rows of white sheep and one black one, worn in 1981, the year she married Prince Charles.
f: The estimate was $50,000–80,000. Bidding jumped from $190,000 in the final fifteen minutes.

d: A 1954 handwritten letter in German in which the physicist calls religion a childish superstition.
The Pink Floyd guitarist's main guitar for decades, heard on the band's landmark albums.
f: It sold for $3.975 million in 2019 and was resold at this sale for more than three times that.

d: The first DBR1 ever built, raced by Stirling Moss among others.
f: It's the most expensive British car ever sold at auction.

house: Toyosu Market New Year auction, Tokyo
d: A bluefin caught off Ōma in northern Japan, sold in the ceremonial first auction of the year.
f: Ōma tuna is widely considered the finest in Japan. Winning the first auction of the year is as much about publicity as about the fish.

d: One of two short-wheelbase supercharged Duesenbergs built. This one was first owned by the film star.

t: Gustav Klimt, Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer
d: A six-foot full-length portrait of the daughter of Klimt's greatest patrons, painted between 1914 and 1916. She wears an imperial Chinese dragon robe.
f: During the war, Lederer claimed Klimt was her real father, a story that helped protect her from Nazi persecution.

d: A rare official reissue of the English charter of liberties, sealed by King Edward I.
One of the most complete T. rex skeletons ever found, named after the amateur palaeontologist who discovered it.
f: It is now on display at a natural history museum in Abu Dhabi.

d: The car that won the 1956 24 Hours of Le Mans, in Ecurie Ecosse blue.
f: It's the most expensive Jaguar ever sold at auction.

d: An exceptionally complete adult stegosaurus found in Colorado, with most of its bones.
f: It sold for about seven times its high estimate, to a hedge-fund billionaire.

t: The $1 Million Canadian Gold Maple Leaf
d: A 100-kilogram coin of pure gold, about half a metre across, with a face value of one million Canadian dollars.
f: Its price was not much above the value of its gold.

d: A sheer gown covered in thousands of hand-sewn crystals, worn by Marilyn Monroe at Madison Square Garden in 1962.
The first book printed in British North America, made in Massachusetts in 1640.
A 38-foot T. rex dug up on a South Dakota cattle ranch between 2021 and 2023. Its skull is so heavy it is displayed separately.
f: The pre-sale estimate was $20–30 million. Seven bidders fought for about ten minutes.

d: One of only two built, named after the engineer who used it as his personal company car.
f: It's the most expensive car ever sold, sold in a sealed auction for invited bidders only.

d: Leonardo's notebook on water, fossils and the moon, written in his mirror-image handwriting.
f: The buyer was Bill Gates.

d: A champion long-distance racing cock, nicknamed the 'Lewis Hamilton of pigeons', sold as a breeding bird.
f: The same anonymous buyer bought New Kim the following year.

d: A gold moon-phase triple-calendar watch with a black diamond-set dial, once owned by Vietnam's last emperor.

t: A Gold Aureus of Brutus, 42 BC
d: A Roman gold coin celebrating the assassination of Julius Caesar, issued by one of the assassins.
One of 170 steel Nautilus watches with a Tiffany-blue dial, made to mark the retailer's 170th anniversary.
f: The retail price was about $52,000.

d: A fully functional toilet cast in solid 18-karat gold, by the artist Maurizio Cattelan. A sister edition was famously stolen from an English palace.
f: It sold in the same evening sale as the record-breaking Klimt.

t: Mahler's Manuscript Score of Symphony No. 2
d: The complete handwritten score of the 'Resurrection' Symphony.
f: It's the most expensive music manuscript ever sold at auction.

t: The Codex Sassoon, a Hebrew Bible
d: The earliest near-complete Hebrew Bible, handwritten on parchment around the year 900.
The 1962 comic that introduced Spider-Man, in near-mint condition.
A complete set of the giant hand-coloured bird prints, each bird shown life-size.
f: This book appears on the list of most expensive books eight separate times.
